correctness.rationale: The coefficient space contains 32767 nonzero equations. For the fibre-quadratic model \(F=U^2A+UVB+V^2C\), singular points lie over roots of B, and the exact two-chart Jacobian criterion is \(\gcd(B,(CA^\prime+AC^\prime)^2+AC(B^\prime)^2)=1\) in both base affine charts. Every equation is classified; the exact \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbf F_2)^2\) group action exhausts 36 transformations and yields 9216 smooth equations and 294 orbits. Independent Groebner bases of (F,dF/du,dF/dt) on all four charts agree for every coordinate orbit representative, smooth and singular. Independent F2,F4,F8 zeta calculations verify all Jacobian 2-ranks on the 294 smooth representatives. Data and scripts are embedded.

value.rationale: The (2,4) divisor is a natural genus-three hyperelliptic model with both rulings distinguished: a unique degree-two cover plus an additional degree-four map. The full 17-cell joint distribution of rational points and Jacobian 2-ranks over F2 and its 294 embedding orbits supplies an arithmetic-incidence invariant that abstract point maxima, general p-rank formulas, and genus-three isomorphism counts do not themselves determine. Particularly 1083 maximal six-point curves split into exactly 282 p-rank-one and 801 ordinary equations (11 and 26 orbits), with a structural proof that other ranks cannot occur. These are natural complete classification data, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice. Neither the elementary six-point bound nor the general p-rank formula is claimed as new.
